questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct for the adiabatic process?
(A)Molar heat capacity is zero.
(B)Molar heat capacity is infinite.
(C)Work done on gas is equal to the increase in internal energy.
(D)The increase in temperature results in a decrease in internal energy.

1. (A) and (C)
2. (B) and (C)
3. (A) and (D)
4. (B) and (D)
questions.explanation:
Hint: In an adiabatic process, heat change is zero. Explanation: (1) In an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, meaning the heat transfer, i.e., 𝑄=0. Since molar heat capacity is defined as⁣ \(\begin{aligned} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{n} \Delta \mathrm{~T}} \end{aligned}\), if 𝑄=0, then 𝐶=0 for any non-zero. (2) According to the first law of thermodynamics, ΔU=Q+W, Δ𝑈 is the change in internal energy, 𝑄 is the heat added to the system, and 𝑊 is the work done by the system. In an adiabatic process, 𝑄=0, so ΔU=W, meaning the increase in internal energy is equal to the work done on the gas. Adiabatic Process \(\rightarrow \mathrm{q}=0\) \(\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{w} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{w} \end{aligned}\) Work done on the gas \(\rightarrow\) Compression \(\rightarrow\) HeatingAn infinite heat capacity would imply no temperature change for any heat input, which contradicts the observed temperature changes in adiabatic processes (e.g., in adiabatic compression, temperature rises). Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.​​​​​​​
